title: Introduce atomic prefetch transaction and minibatch scheduler rewrite
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Replace the current ad-hoc prefetch + eviction dance with a single atomic prefetch transaction and rewrite the minibatch scheduler to remove priority inversion, reduce head-of-line blocking, and simplify lease semantics. Scope: runtime serving components: prefetcher, KV cache lease manager, minibatch scheduler, and admission controller. Non-goals: model runtime kernel changes, API surface changes, or customer-facing semantics (this is internal optimization only). Constraints: must preserve current latency SLOs for p50/p95/p99 and provide a clear rollback path behind feature flag 'atomic_prefetch_v1'. Must be compatible with Dedicated and Hosted variants; Private deployments must be opt-in via config. Key risks: transient cache warmup regressions, GC pauses during migration, and scheduler starvation for long-seq sessions. Mitigations and trade-offs are documented below.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests for atomic prefetch transaction (deterministic replay harness)
E2E benchmark: p95 token generation latency not worse than 5% under 99th percentile load compared to baseline
KV cache hit ratio improves or stays within 1% of baseline after warmup on representative workloads
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with automatic rollback if tail latency exceeds threshold
Code review approvals from runtime, infra, and reliability teams; compiled release notes and migration instructions
metrics_targets: p99_tail_latency: no more than baseline + 10ms absolute
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature branch validation and local deterministic replay (complete). Phase 1: deploy behind 'atomic_prefetch_v1' to internal canary fleet (10 nodes) and run synthetic benchmark suites + production shadowing (expected 3 days). Phase 2: 5% traffic canary for 24h with automated p95/p99 guardrails in Grafana (rollback on breach). Phase 3: 25% for 48h, confirm telemetry and cost delta. Phase 4: 100% with fast rollback and post-rollout regression evals. If any regression seen, revert flag and run postmortem. Use canary tags: canary/atomic-prefetch-2026-03.
comments: 2026-02-16 — Aisha Khan: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to make prefetch operations transactional to avoid double-eviction during requeue. Action: prototype transaction record in in-memory MVCC map.

2026-02-22 — Marco Delrio: Implemented prototype in branch 'atomic-prefetch/proto'. Observed 6% improvement in cache hit for short-context workloads but a 2.4% p95 regression under taily multi-tenant load. Added additional metrics to track 'prefetch_txn_latency' and 'txn_conflicts'.

2026-02-26 — Review by Priya Singh (Reliability): flagged risk of GC pressure from extra transient objects in transaction staging area. Suggest switching from std::vector allocations to arena pool or slab allocator.

2026-03-01 — Marco Delrio: Switched to arena allocator and re-ran harness: p95 regression reduced to 1.1% and txn_conflicts reduced by 70%. Added unit tests for conflict resolution and deterministic ordering.

2026-03-03 — UX (observability) sync: agreed to add new dashboard panels: 'prefetch_txn_rate', 'txn_conflict_ratio', and 'minibatch_wait_time' in grafana/serving-runtime. Dashboards PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/grafana-dashboards/pull/217

2026-03-06 — Security review requested by Marco: no customer data leaves process; KMS path unchanged. Security (Jon Park) commented: ensure audit logs include txn start/commit/abort IDs for Private deployments. Added audit hook for Private in PR-4782.

2026-03-09 — Load test: running multi-tenant blast with 2x baseline QPS for 6h. Observed steady state: throughput -0.3%, p95 +0.9%, cache hit +1.8%. Opening this ticket for follow-ups: optimize lease heartbeats and add backpressure windowing to reduce latency spikes.
